title: Proverbs Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Proverbs chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Proverbs Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Proverbs Chapter 21.

questions.question: In Proverbs 21, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD
To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
An high look, and a proud heart, and the plowing of the wicked, is sin.
The way of man is froward and strange.
questions.correctAnswer: The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD
questions.explanation: This is stated in Proverbs 21:1, making it the first statement in the chapter.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 21:2 say about a man's way?
options: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes
questions.correctAnswer: Both A and B
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:2 states that every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the LORD pondereth the hearts.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 21:3, what is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice?
questions.correctAnswer: To do justice and judgment
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:3 clearly states that to do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.

questions.question: What three things are mentioned in Proverbs 21:4 as being sin?
options: An high look, a proud heart, and the plowing of the wicked
A proud heart, deceit, and anger
questions.correctAnswer: An high look, a proud heart, and the plowing of the wicked
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:4 states that these three are sin.

questions.question: What do the thoughts of the diligent tend to, according to Proverbs 21:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Plenteousness
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:5 indicates that the thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness.

questions.question: What is described as vanity in Proverbs 21:6?
options: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue
questions.correctAnswer: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:6 states that this is vanity tossed to and fro of those that seek death.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 21:7, what shall destroy the wicked?
questions.correctAnswer: Their refusal to do judgment
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:7 states that the robbery of the wicked shall destroy them because they refuse to do judgment.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 21:8 say about the way of man?
questions.correctAnswer: It is froward and strange
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:8 describes the way of man as froward and strange.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 21:9 suggest about dwelling with a brawling woman?
options: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop
It is preferable to share a large house
It is a sign of strength
questions.correctAnswer: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:9 states that it is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop than with a brawling woman in a wide house.

questions.question: What does the soul of the wicked desire, according to Proverbs 21:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Evil
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:10 states that the soul of the wicked desireth evil.

questions.question: What happens when the scorner is punished, according to Proverbs 21:11?
questions.correctAnswer: The simple is made wise
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:11 indicates that when the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise.

questions.question: True or False: The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is a fact stated in Proverbs 21:1.

questions.question: True or False: The way of man is described as just and right in Proverbs 21.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:8 indicates that the way of man is froward and strange, thus not just and right.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 21 states that all men are wicked.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not say that all men are wicked; it contrasts the wicked with the pure and diligent.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD finds every man's way acceptable in Proverbs 21.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:2 states that every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the LORD pondereth the hearts, indicating not all ways are acceptable.

medium.title: Proverbs Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Proverbs Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 21:12, what does God do to the wicked for their wickedness?
options: God blesseth the wicked for their wickedness
God overthroweth the wicked for their wickedness
God ignorreth the wicked for their wickedness
God rewardeth the wicked for their wickedness
questions.correctAnswer: God overthroweth the wicked for their wickedness
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:12 states that God overthroweth the wicked for their wickedness, showing divine judgment against evil actions.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 21:13 promise will happen if someone stops his ears at the cry of the poor (Proverbs 21:13)?
options: He shall cry himself, but shall not be heard
He shall find peace and rest
He shall prosper in all his ways
questions.correctAnswer: He shall cry himself, but shall not be heard
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:13 promises that if someone stops his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard, indicating consequences for ignoring the needy.

questions.question: What effect does a gift in secret have according to Proverbs 21:14?
questions.correctAnswer: It pacifieth anger
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:14 explains that a gift in secret pacifieth anger, showing how discreet generosity can calm fury.

questions.question: What is the relationship between loving pleasure and wealth according to Proverbs 21:17 and 21:20?
options: Loving pleasure leads to riches, and the wise man wastes treasure
Loving pleasure leads to poverty, but the wise man stores treasure
Loving pleasure leads to wisdom, and the foolish man saves treasure
Loving pleasure leads to honor, and the wise man spends all
questions.correctAnswer: Loving pleasure leads to poverty, but the wise man stores treasure
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:17 says he that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man, while Proverbs 21:20 states the wise man stores treasure and oil, contrasting the consequences of indulgence versus wisdom.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 21:15, what is the outcome for those who do judgment justly?
options: It is joy to the just to do judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It is joy to the just to do judgment
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:15 highlights that it is joy to the just to do judgment, emphasizing the righteous delight in fairness.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 21:19 advise about living with an angry woman?
options: It is better to dwell in the wilderness
It is better to live in a large house
It is better to live in the city
It is better to dwell with friends
questions.correctAnswer: It is better to dwell in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:19 teaches that it is better to dwell in the wilderness than with a contentious and angry woman, showing the value of peace over comfort.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 21:21, what can one find by following righteousness and mercy?
questions.correctAnswer: Life, righteousness, and honour
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:21 states that he that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour, highlighting the blessings of godly living.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 21:22 say a wise man can do?
options: Scaleth the city of the mighty and casteth down their confidence
questions.correctAnswer: Scaleth the city of the mighty and casteth down their confidence
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:22 describes how a wise man scaleth the city of the mighty and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof, illustrating the power of wisdom.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Proverbs 21:16 for the man who wanders out of the way of understanding?
options: He shall remain in the congregation of the dead
questions.correctAnswer: He shall remain in the congregation of the dead
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:16 warns that the man who wanders out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead, indicating spiritual death or ruin.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 21:18 describe the wicked in relation to the righteous?
options: The wicked shall be a ransom for the righteous
The wicked shall be blessed with the righteous
The wicked shall inherit the same blessings as the righteous
The wicked shall be ignored by the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked shall be a ransom for the righteous
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:18 states that the wicked shall be a ransom for the righteous, indicating the substitutionary consequences of wickedness.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 21:20 say about the treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise?
options: They are wasted by the wise
There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise
They bring sorrow to the wise
questions.correctAnswer: There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:20 praises the wise for having treasure and oil in their dwelling, implying prudent stewardship and resourcefulness.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 21:13 warn will happen to someone who stops his ears at the cry of the poor?
options: He will be blessed with riches
He shall cry himself, but shall not be heard
He will gain favor with God
questions.correctAnswer: He shall cry himself, but shall not be heard
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:13 warns that ignoring the poor results in the person himself crying out but not being heard, showing the principle of divine justice.

questions.question: What is the practical teaching of Proverbs 21:14 regarding anger?
options: A reward in the bosom increases wrath
A gift in secret pacifieth anger
questions.correctAnswer: A gift in secret pacifieth anger
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:14 teaches that a gift given secretly can calm anger, suggesting tactful generosity can resolve conflicts.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 21:21 says that following righteousness and mercy leads to life, righteousness, and honor.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:21 clearly states that he who follows righteousness and mercy finds life, righteousness, and honor.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 21:19 recommends living with a contentious and angry woman over dwelling in the wilderness.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:19 states it is better to dwell in the wilderness than with a contentious and angry woman, advising against such company.

hard.title: Proverbs Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Proverbs Chapter 21.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 21:23, what does one keep by guarding their mouth and tongue?
questions.correctAnswer: His soul from troubles
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:23 states, 'Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles,' indicating the protection of one's soul through careful speech.

questions.question: In Proverbs 21:24, how is the proud and haughty scorner described?
options: One who deals in proud wrath
questions.correctAnswer: One who deals in proud wrath
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:24 calls the proud and haughty scorner 'his name, who dealeth in proud wrath,' highlighting his arrogant and wrathful nature.

questions.question: What is the consequence for the slothful according to Proverbs 21:25?
options: The desire of the slothful killeth him
The slothful shall inherit the earth
The desire of the slothful is fulfilled
questions.correctAnswer: The desire of the slothful killeth him
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:25 explains that 'The desire of the slothful killeth him; for his hands refuse to labour,' showing the fatal effect of laziness.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 21:26, how does the righteous person behave in contrast to the covetous?
options: The righteous giveth and spareth not
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous giveth and spareth not
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:26 contrasts the covetous who 'coveteth greedily all the day long' with the righteous who 'giveth and spareth not,' emphasizing generosity.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 21:27 say about the sacrifice of the wicked brought with a wicked mind?
questions.correctAnswer: It is an abomination
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:27 states, 'The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?' demonstrating the rejection of insincere offerings.

questions.question: What is the fate of a false witness according to Proverbs 21:28?
questions.correctAnswer: Shall perish
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:28 declares, 'A false witness shall perish,' indicating the severe consequences for bearing false testimony.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'chamad' (חמד) in Proverbs 21:26 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To covet greedily
questions.explanation: The Hebrew verb 'chamad' translated as 'coveteth greedily' in Proverbs 21:26 means to desire or covet something intensely or greedily.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Proverbs 21:23, 'Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles'?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:23 uses synonymous parallelism, repeating the concept of guarding speech to emphasize protection from troubles.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse echoes the theme of Proverbs 21:1 about the LORD directing the hearts of kings?
questions.correctAnswer: Acts 13:22
questions.explanation: Acts 13:22 references King David, showing God’s sovereign guidance over kings, echoing Proverbs 21:1 about the LORD turning the king's heart.

questions.question: Which passage in Psalms aligns with Proverbs 21:31 that safety is from the LORD despite preparation?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 20:7
questions.explanation: Psalm 20:7 contrasts trust in chariots and horses with trust in the name of the LORD, paralleling Proverbs 21:31's theme that safety is of the LORD.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Proverbs 21:23?
questions.correctAnswer: Proverbs 21:22
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:22 immediately precedes 21:23 and speaks about a wise man scaling the city of the mighty, setting context for the counsel about speech in 21:23.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 21:30 challenge human wisdom?
options: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD
Human wisdom is greater than divine counsel
Wisdom comes from the wise alone
Counsel is unnecessary for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:30 explicitly states that no human wisdom, understanding, or counsel can stand against the LORD, emphasizing divine supremacy.

questions.question: What is the literary significance of the contrast between the wicked and the upright in Proverbs 21:29?
questions.correctAnswer: Antithetic parallelism
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:29 contrasts the wicked hardening his face with the upright directing his way, an example of antithetic parallelism, highlighting opposing behaviors.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 21:25 and 21:26, what two opposing character traits are illustrated?
questions.correctAnswer: Slothfulness and greediness
questions.explanation: Verses 25 and 26 discuss the slothful desire that kills and the greedy covetousness all day long, illustrating laziness versus greed.

questions.question: What cultural context helps explain the warning in Proverbs 21:27 about the sacrifice of the wicked?
options: Sacrifices required purity of heart and intention
Sacrifices were only performed by priests
Sacrifices could be given anytime without restrictions
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrifices required purity of heart and intention
questions.explanation: In ancient Israel, sacrifices were not merely ritual but required sincere, pure intentions; Proverbs 21:27 condemns wicked sacrifices with a wicked mind, reflecting this cultural-religious norm.

theological.title: Proverbs Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Proverbs Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Proverbs 21:2 teach about human sin and divine judgment?
options: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the LORD pondereth the hearts
God overlooks human sin when it is done unknowingly
Human righteousness is sufficient for justification
Man’s external actions are the primary focus of divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the LORD pondereth the hearts
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:2 highlights that humans often justify themselves, but God judges the inner motives, showing the doctrine of God’s omniscient judgment of the heart.

questions.question: What doctrine does Proverbs 21:3 teach about the relationship between justice and worship?
options: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice
Sacrifices alone ensure God's favor despite injustice
Worship rituals are more important than ethical behavior
Justice is optional if one offers proper sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:3 teaches that God values ethical living and justice above ritual sacrifice, emphasizing the primacy of moral obedience over ceremonial acts.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human diligence and divine blessing is taught in Proverbs 21:5?
options: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want
Wealth is guaranteed by human effort alone
Haste is a virtue that leads to success
Divine blessing is unrelated to human planning
questions.correctAnswer: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want
questions.explanation: This verse teaches the doctrine that God blesses diligent, wise planning whereas rashness leads to want, highlighting sanctification in wise stewardship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Proverbs 21:1 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:1 shows God’s sovereignty as He directs the king’s heart like rivers of water, illustrating His control over human affairs.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Proverbs 21:30 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:30 declares there is no wisdom or counsel against the LORD, affirming His omnipotence and ultimate authority over all.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 21:21 connect to the broader biblical theme of sanctification and eternal reward?
options: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour
Sanctification is optional for receiving eternal life
Mercy is unrelated to righteous living
Honor is only earthly and temporary
questions.correctAnswer: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour
questions.explanation: This verse anticipates New Testament teaching that pursuing righteousness and mercy leads to true life and honor, a key theme in sanctification.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 21:31 relate to New Testament trust in divine providence in times of conflict?
options: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the LORD
Human effort alone secures victory without God’s help
God’s providence is irrelevant in battle
questions.correctAnswer: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the LORD
questions.explanation: This verse connects to New Testament themes of trusting in God’s providence rather than mere human strength for ultimate safety.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 21:3 and Proverbs 21:15 teach about justice and divine judgment?
options: Doing justice pleases God more than sacrifice, and justice brings joy to the just but destruction to workers of iniquity
Sacrifices are more important than justice
Justice is irrelevant to divine judgment
Workers of iniquity receive joy from God
questions.correctAnswer: Doing justice pleases God more than sacrifice, and justice brings joy to the just but destruction to workers of iniquity
questions.explanation: These verses together teach that God values just living over ritual and that justice leads to blessing while injustice leads to destruction.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 21:2 and Proverbs 21:29 teach about human sin and righteousness?
options: Man’s ways seem right to himself, but God judges the heart; the wicked harden their faces, but the upright direct their way
External appearance is the true measure of righteousness
God overlooks the hardness of the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Man’s ways seem right to himself, but God judges the heart; the wicked harden their faces, but the upright direct their way
questions.explanation: These verses show human self-deception versus divine judgment and contrast the stubborn wicked with the upright who follow God’s direction.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 21:13 and Proverbs 21:14 teach about mercy and social justice?
options: Ignoring the cry of the poor results in God’s judgment, but a secret gift pacifies anger and wrath
Ignoring the poor has no consequences
Anger cannot be pacified by gifts
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring the cry of the poor results in God’s judgment, but a secret gift pacifies anger and wrath
questions.explanation: Together, these verses teach God’s concern for social justice and the power of discreet mercy to calm conflict.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Proverbs 21:6–7 promotes deceit and robbery as acceptable means to wealth. What does this passage actually teach?
options: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death; the robbery of the wicked shall destroy them
Deceit is a wise strategy for gaining wealth
Robbery is condoned for the wicked
Wealth obtained by deceit is blessed by God
questions.correctAnswer: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death; the robbery of the wicked shall destroy them
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:6–7 condemns deceit and robbery, warning that such acts lead to destruction, not blessing.

questions.question: What doctrine does Proverbs 21:12 teach about divine justice against wickedness?
options: The righteous wisely consider the house of the wicked, but God overthroweth the wicked for their wickedness
God ignores the wicked when the righteous act
The wicked prosper despite their sin
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous wisely consider the house of the wicked, but God overthroweth the wicked for their wickedness
questions.explanation: This verse teaches that God actively judges and overthrows the wicked, while the righteous perceive their downfall.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exhibited in Proverbs 21:28 regarding truth and justice?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:28 shows God’s justice by stating that false witnesses perish, emphasizing divine retribution for falsehood.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 21:20 and Proverbs 21:26 teach about wisdom and wealth stewardship?
options: The wise store treasures and oil, but the foolish spend it all; the righteous give generously, while the covetous desire greedily
Covetousness is a mark of righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: The wise store treasures and oil, but the foolish spend it all; the righteous give generously, while the covetous desire greedily
questions.explanation: These verses teach the doctrine that wisdom involves prudent saving and generous giving, contrasting with foolishness and greed.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 21:16 connect to biblical teaching on the consequences of rejecting wisdom?
options: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead
Wisdom is optional for spiritual life
Understanding does not affect one’s ultimate destiny
questions.correctAnswer: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead
questions.explanation: This verse aligns with biblical teaching that rejecting wisdom results in spiritual death and separation from the living.
